title: Answer the Center Pawn
setup: White has pushed a second pawn to the center, where it attacks your pawn on e5.
hint: Your e-pawn is attacked. Which answer removes White's center pawn instead of just defending?
explanation:
## The Idea

White's pawn on d4 attacks your pawn on e5. {{exd4}} takes it, and White has only one center pawn left. If White takes back with {{Qxd4}}, that is the Center Game, and {{Nc6}} hits the queen with a developing move.

Ignore the offer instead, and {{dxe5}} wins your pawn or a push to d5 gains space.

When a center pawn is attacked, trading it for the attacker is often the cleanest answer.
